problem: The same-route NL/EN fix was correct in intent but made the production build undeployable because tools/site-shell/apply-i18n.mjs contained a malformed String.replace expression.
root_cause: The legacy mobile CTA injection path was edited into `mobileLanguage + 'MOBILE_LANGUAGE + '$&''`, which is invalid JavaScript. The i18n authority regression checked route semantics but did not compile the actual build injector, so the syntax defect escaped pre-merge semantic tests and Netlify failed before deployment.
fix: Restore the replacement expression to `mobileLanguage + '$&'` so the generated language switcher is inserted immediately before the matched CTA.
Add `node --check tools/site-shell/apply-i18n.mjs` as an executable regression.
Align the older global i18n test with the canonical route-link architecture instead of the retired select-based injector.
Keep same-page NL/EN route generation and production browser round-trip verification fail-closed.
prevention: Every JavaScript build-time transformer modified by a candidate must be syntax-compiled before protected merge.
Semantic string assertions are not a substitute for parsing/executing the build script.
Static public locale navigation remains route-link based: /prijzen ↔ /en/prijzen, /systemen-koppelen ↔ /en/systemen-koppelen, and / ↔ /en.
A production deploy failure remains non-green until exact-main deploy and browser readback pass.
